parsed.explanation: Outed visitors face state threat-framing as a national-defense risk, selective imprisonment up to 2 years under the 2026 penal code, provincial caning, police venue raids and extortion, and recent vigilante attacks on trans women tied to official rhetoric. A disputed death-in-custody trans-traveller case, with alleged beating and $100,000 release demand, shows custody can be lethal, though no execution or trans-specific prosecution under the new code is documented. No operative anti-discrimination protection is shown. Uncertainty remains on enforcement frequency, but documented targeting dominates.

entry_documents.exposure: Airport arrest of trans traveller in 2022 and document/presentation mismatch risk documented; no specific foreign-document or X-marker rule stated.
entry_documents.interaction: Airport arrest led to custody, alleged extortion and death, escalating a document or drug encounter into detention exposure.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Death in custody after airport arrest; mother alleges beating and $100,000 demand, police deny violence; venue raids detain dozens, rehabilitation raids detain trans women.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: No documented effective consular, legal-aid or complaint remedy for visitors.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Police detention interacts with weak recourse and alleged extortion, making release and safety uncertain.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Aceh Islamic code canes a person with gender disorder; local fines on trans women; facilities and placement rules for visitors not documented.
federal_state_facilities.protection: National police sometimes refuse local rules conflicting with national guarantees, but application varies locally.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: National penal code plus provincial criminalisation and local bylaws create a combined, locally variable regime.

care_services.exposure: Care access, HRT import and hospital placement for visitors not documented; psychiatric pathologisation in 2016 signals hostile institutional posture.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: 2026 penal code effectively criminalises same-sex relations, up to 2 years, selective prosecution; 2025 decree lists LGBTQ+ people as national-defense threats; pornography law up to 7 years.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: 2015 police circular and 2009 minority-protection regulation exist but outcomes not sourced; constitutional guarantee is theoretical.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official threat-framing and morality laws licence police raids and vigilante action described in 2026 reporting.

minors_guardians.interaction: Officials called on parents to monitor children in 'this lifestyle' in July 2026, but no traveller-facing minor or guardian rule is documented.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: August 2026 vigilante mobs attacked trans women, tied to officials' rhetoric and defense decree; 94 LGBT abuse cases documented in 2026 report.
street_violence_police_response.protection: No documented prosecution of attackers or effective police protection for trans victims.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: State rhetoric, vigilante violence and police raids reinforce each other rather than police restraining attackers.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No specific anti-discrimination protection as of 2019; enforcement of police protective circulars, new-code use against trans visitors, and death-case facts remain unresolved.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Human-rights commission advice once rescinded a discriminatory job offer, but no traveller remedy is documented.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Paper protections without documented operating remedy do not offset documented raids, extortion and mob attacks.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar in routine police power, custody abuse and illusory remedies, but here imprisonment is selective rather than highly likely after discovery and no capital pathway is documented, so it sits above the 0.15 anchor.

Similar raids, fines, extortion and short detention with rare imprisonment, but recent vigilante attacks explicitly linked to a national-defense threat decree and a disputed custodial death push it below 0.25.
Both involve discretionary stops, fines and weak courts, but this case adds criminalised same-sex conduct, caning, mob violence and death in custody, so it is materially below 0.35.

parsed.synthesis: The combined regime is hostile at every stage: national law criminalises the conduct a trans visitor with a same-sex partner may be imputed with, provinces add caning, and official defense-threat framing coincides with vigilante attacks and police raids. Detention can involve extortion and alleged lethal abuse without documented remedy. Variation and selective prosecution create uncertainty about frequency, not about severity if outed, placing the jurisdiction at the severe end of high risk.
